results.title: Coroutines and Tasks — Python documentation
results.snippet: Task.cancel() arranges for a CancelledError to be thrown into the wrapped coroutine at the next opportunity. It does not guarantee that the task will be cancelled: the coroutine may suppress the exception.

results.title: How to Cancel an Asyncio Task
results.snippet: Cancellation is cooperative. A task that never awaits cannot be cancelled, and a shield created with asyncio.shield() protects its inner awaitable from the request.

results.title: asyncio: CancelledError swallowed by a bare except in a finally block
results.snippet: Catching Exception in a coroutine's cleanup path will not catch CancelledError, which inherits from BaseException since Python 3.8 precisely so that cancellation is not swallowed by accident.
